humanities_role_explanation: The humanities material (classical Islamic literature) acts as a highly challenging text corpus to test machine translation and OCR capabilities, rather than testing disciplinary humanistic reasoning. The performance is evaluated using automated linguistic metrics (semantic vector similarity) rather than expert domain-specific analysis.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: The primary task is Arabic-to-English text translation. However, the pipeline also evaluates image-to-text OCR of classical Arabic book pages using multi-modal LLMs.
analytical_tasks_explanation: The pipeline performs forward and backward machine translation (translation), OCR transcription of image-based PDFs including diacritic preservation (transcription_and_correction), and vector-based RAG matching to align transcribed passages with authoritative databases of sacred texts (retrieval_and_ranking).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The paper does not present a general-purpose benchmark, but rather a specialized pipeline and evaluation for translating Islamic scholarly texts.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates generative LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Claude 3 Haiku.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses cosine similarity of vector embeddings to measure semantic equivalence of back-translations, alongside human acceptance rates.

summary: This paper presents an automated pipeline designed to translate classical Arabic Islamic literature from the Al-Shamela Library into English and other languages. The authors address domain-specific challenges by utilizing multi-modal LLMs for Arabic OCR, applying RAG to maintain the textual integrity of Quranic and Hadith verses, and validating quality through automated back-translation semantic similarity and human crowd-sourced reviews.
key_findings: Using embedding-based semantic similarity, 71% of translations validated via GPT-4o-mini back-translation and 86% of translations validated via Claude 3 Haiku back-translation achieved acceptable quality scores (cosine similarity >= 0.7).
facets_explanation: The reference texts used for translation and back-translation validation are sourced from the pre-existing Al-Shamela digital library database. Automated evaluation compares the model's back-translation against a single original Arabic page reference using vector-embedding cosine similarity. For the manual validation portion, human annotator divergence is treated as noise, requiring a consensus of at least two reviewers to accept any translation errors.
